summary_alerts.html:
CONSENSUS BUY — GOOGL (Khanna (D) + Capito (R) + Fetterman (D) + Taylor (R) + Keating (D), cross-party)
5 members, combined disclosed value ~$72K. Five members spanning both parties and both chambers accumulated Alphabet shares during the window, representing the strongest cross-party consensus buy signal of the cycle. The breadth of accumulation across Democrats and Republicans alike may reflect collective confidence in Alphabet's AI infrastructure positioning and continued advertising revenue resilience.

CONSENSUS BUY — HD (Khanna (D) + McCormick (R) + Taylor (R), cross-party)
3 members, combined disclosed value ~$132K. Three members from both parties disclosed Home Depot purchases totaling ~$132K, with Khanna driving the majority of disclosed value through repeated accumulation on two separate dates. This cross-party convergence on a leading home improvement retailer may indicate shared expectations of resilient consumer spending in the housing and renovation segment.

CONSENSUS BUY — AMZN (Khanna (D) + Taylor (R) + Fetterman (D), cross-party)
3 members, combined disclosed value ~$97K. Three cross-party members disclosed Amazon purchases during the window, with Khanna adding shares across three separate dates, suggesting sustained conviction in the name. The bipartisan interest may reflect continued confidence in Amazon's cloud infrastructure and e-commerce platform amid broader technology sector volatility.

CONSENSUS SELL — AAPL (Suozzi (D) + Taylor (R) + Khanna (D), cross-party)
3 members, combined disclosed value ~$48K. Three members across party lines disclosed Apple sales totaling approximately $48K, with Suozzi registering the largest individual position (~$32K on February 18). This cross-party exit pattern may reflect profit-taking at elevated valuations or caution ahead of anticipated pressure on consumer hardware demand.

CONSENSUS SELL — WAT (Khanna (D) + Dingell (D) + Hern (R), cross-party)
3 members, combined disclosed value ~$48K. Waters Corporation—an analytical instruments manufacturer serving pharmaceutical and life sciences clients—drew coordinated selling from three members across party lines during the window. The sell pattern may signal reduced near-term conviction in life sciences instrumentation, potentially linked to softening capital expenditure from pharmaceutical customers.

CONSENSUS SELL — T (Fetterman (D) + Taylor (R) + Khanna (D), cross-party)
3 members, combined disclosed value ~$24K. Three cross-party members reduced or exited AT&T positions during the window, accumulating $24K in combined disclosed sell value. The pattern may reflect persistent skepticism about the telecom sector's growth trajectory, particularly given ongoing concerns around AT&T's debt obligations and competitive pressures in wireless broadband.

CONVICTION — Kevin Hern TXN ~$750K
Rep. Kevin Hern (R-OK) disclosed the largest single-member transaction in this window—a ~$750K sale of Texas Instruments on March 18, 2026, representing approximately 41% of his total disclosed sell volume for the period. The scale and concentration of this liquidation in a leading analog semiconductor company with broad industrial and automotive exposure may warrant monitoring as a sector-specific risk signal.
